prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: API 错误码排查对照表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "错误码" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 49px
  col 2: header "错误信息" · longest unbreakable word 154px · one-line width 154px
  col 3: header "含义" · longest unbreakable word 95px · one-line width 740px
  col 4: header "解决办法" · longest unbreakable word 110px · one-line width 1964px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [70, 175, 116, 230] · table 592×1733px · row heights [36, 222, 246, 222, 246, 246, 246, 269] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 232px
Design r1C: widths [70, 175, 125, 300] · table 671×1407px · row heights [36, 222, 199, 199, 176, 199, 176, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 311px
Design r2A: widths [70, 175, 135, 285] · table 666×1384px · row heights [36, 199, 199, 176, 199, 199, 176, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 306px
Design r2B: widths [70, 175, 114, 280] · table 640×1454px · row heights [36, 222, 199, 199, 199, 199, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 1 · OVERFLOWS the box by 280px
Design r2C: widths [70, 175, 155, 300] · table 701×1337px · row heights [36, 176, 199, 176, 176, 199, 176, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 341px
Design r3A: widths [70, 175, 130, 300] · table 676×1361px · row heights [36, 199, 199, 176, 176, 199, 176, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 316px
Design r3B: widths [70, 175, 120, 270] · table 636×1500px · row heights [36, 222, 222, 199, 199, 199, 199, 222] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 276px
Design r3C: widths [70, 175, 135, 330] · table 711×1244px · row heights [36, 199, 176, 176, 153, 176, 153, 176] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 351px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3A"],"acceptable":["r1B","r1C","r2A","r2C","r3B","r3C"],"bad":[{"design":"r2B","why":"“access_token”被拆到两行，破坏了排查时需要辨认的技术标识符；仅比 r3A 少 36px 的横向宽度，却增加了表格高度。"}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[70,72],[175,180],[125,135],[285,310]],"rationale":"r3A 保持错误码和错误信息完整，给含义列足够宽度容纳技术词，同时让篇幅最长的解决办法有更宽的阅读空间。行高相对均衡，纵向浏览的负担也比更窄的方案小。手机初始视口能看见完整的前两列和部分含义，但阅读完整含义及解决办法仍需横向滚动。","principles":{"general":["优先保持用于检索和识别的代码、标识符完整，再按正文的篇幅和阅读用途分配剩余宽度。","评估横向滚动时，应同时看初始视口能提供什么信息，以及滚动后各列是否易于阅读。","行高应结合各列内容的换行和留白判断；更短的表格不一定更易读。"],"specific":["本表的错误信息列至少需要约 175px 才能容纳最长标识符；错误码列约 70px 即可完整显示。","解决办法的内容远长于含义，分配明显更宽的列有助于控制行高。"]},"tradeoffs":"r1B 和 r3B 的横向滚动距离较短，但行更高；r3C 的解决办法更宽、表格更短，但横向滚动更远。r2C 为含义提供更多阅读宽度，也相应增加了滚动距离。","uncertain":"偏重初始视口完整显示含义列的设计师可能选择 r1B 或 r3B；偏重阅读解决办法的设计师可能选择 r3C。给出的范围是围绕 r3A 的保守视觉估计，并非逐像素实测；各列同时变化时仍需重新检查换行和滚动效果。"}
